short: A 16-bit number format widely used to train AI models — it saves memory while keeping the wide range needed for stable training.
definition: bfloat16 (brain floating point) is a compact 16-bit format for storing the numbers inside a neural network, designed by Google for AI workloads. Compared with the standard 32-bit format, it halves memory use and speeds up computation, letting bigger models train on the same hardware. Its trick is keeping the same wide range of magnitudes as 32-bit numbers while giving up some fine precision — a tradeoff that turns out to keep training stable, which is why it became a default for training large models. It is typically used alongside higher-precision math in what's called mixed-precision training.
